replica_rule: replica r: numpy default_rng(r) bootstrap of the 30 train files (counts in the closed form; theta on the first n_sub distinct drawn files); validation and test fixed
eval_rule: validation and (report-only) test every max(500, steps/40) steps; selection only by validation
title: Ablation: why Kerr with memory + off-axis triplets beats triplets alone
question: At equal RM (about 430, 1200, 2200), which part gives the gain of A1 over the full triplet table: the memory of the Kerr phase, the off-axis triplets, or the exponential (all-order, constrained) form of the axial terms?

code_facts.T: e046_fit.job_terms('T') = triplet_terms(M, 'T3') + FIR7: all merged terms m <= n with |m+n| <= M, INCLUDING the axial ones (m = 0 or n = 0: x_k |x_{k+j}|^2, j = -M..M, 2M+1 terms) and the centre (0,0), free complex coefficients
code_facts.Kerr: kerr_offaxis.Kerr: u = FIR7(x), y = u exp(-i sum_{j=-r..r} alpha_j |u_{k+j}|^2), alpha real and symmetric (alpha_j = alpha_-j), N_c = 2r + 1 taps; first order: the axial terms x_k |x_{k+j}|^2 for |j| <= r with purely imaginary coefficients symmetric in j, plus all higher orders of the same phase
code_facts.offaxis: kerr_offaxis.offaxis_terms(M) = T3 terms with m != 0 and n != 0; m + n = 0 IS included (e.g. (-1, 1): x_{k-1} x_{k+1} conj(x_k))

arms.1: all triplets (T, E046 M3/5/8 and E048 M11/15; existing)
arms.2: Kerr without memory (N_c = 1) + off-axis (A1 varpro N_c = 1; NEW in E056)
arms.3: Kerr with memory, no off-axis (K seq N_c 7/15/31 E046, 31/63 E048; existing)
arms.4: Kerr with memory + off-axis (A1 varpro E046/E048; existing)
arms.5: control: Kerr without memory, no off-axis (K seq N_c = 1; NEW in E056)

rule_draft.level_choice: per arm and RM level: the configuration (M, N_c, pruning set, lambda) with RM <= level * 1.05 and the best mean validation over 5 replicas; test reported (mean, SE, std)
rule_draft.memory_effect: arm 4 - arm 2 at the same level > 2 SE and > 2 std: memory of the Kerr phase matters
rule_draft.offaxis_effect: arm 4 - arm 3 (best Kerr-only, any RM <= level) > 2 SE and > 2 std: off-axis terms matter
rule_draft.form_effect: arm 2 - arm 1 at the same level > 2 SE and > 2 std: the exponential instantaneous Kerr + off-axis beats free axial coefficients
rule_draft.limits: 5 bootstrap replicas of the train files (closed form), one split (E004); Kerr-only arms have one fixed RM each (35-66), they cannot be placed at higher levels
